report.source_text: The slides were fixed by Spray-Cyte and sent to the Pathology Laboratory, which showed that the patient’s sample was positive for malignancy, since there were clusters of malignant epithelial cells with enlarged hyperchromatic pleomorphic nuclei with coarse chromatin. Cell-block immunostaining showed positive reactivity of the malignant cells to CK-7, TTF-1, and focally for Napsin-A. These findings indicated primary lung adenocarcinoma.

report.source_text: The patient was admitted to the hospital for a malignancy workup with weakness in the left side of the body. Dexamethasone was started at a loading dose of 10 mg intravenously and continued on a regular dose, and levetiracetam 500 mg orally was started for prophylaxis to prevent convulsions. The patient followed up with the Oncology Department for staging and prognosis. Afterward, the patient was referred to the Palliative Care team.

clinician.final_diagnosis: The patient had stage IV metastatic lung adenocarcinoma.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old man with a 30-pack-year smoking history presented with left-sided weakness, headache, and constitutional symptoms. Brain CT revealed lesions in the right parietal lobe. Chest CT showed a mass in the right upper lobe, and abdominal CT showed multiple hypodense liver lesions. Biopsy confirmed primary lung adenocarcinoma. Molecular testing results were not reported. The patient received symptomatic treatment with Dexamethasone and Levetiracetam, was followed by Oncology for staging and prognosis, and subsequently referred to Palliative Care. No further clinical course or outcome was documented.
